thought.text: The earlier SIGPIPE interrupted the extraction. Let me extract cleanly.

reasoning_content:
Exit code 2 means that `ls -d elasticsearch-7.17.28` failed, i.e., the extraction did not produce the directory. In other words, the previous tar extraction had not completed (the error occurred first). Let's check the state and re-extract. Exit code 141 (SIGPIPE) from the `file`/tar pipe... Actually, that earlier error occurred on a compound command: `file && tar -tzf | head -3 && echo && tar -xzf && ls`. The "TAR_OK" message was not displayed. In other words, `tar -tzf ... | head -3` caused a SIGPIPE. It's possible that head closed the pipe early, tar received SIGPIPE and exited with 141, and since the `&&` chain was broken, the full extraction `tar -xzf` was not executed.

Let's properly re-run the extraction without using a pipe to head.

action.command: cd /opt/downloads && tar -xzf elasticsearch-7.17.28-linux-x86_64.tar.gz; echo "EXIT:$?"; ls -d elasticsearch-7.17.28 && ls elasticsearch-7.17.28/bin | tr '\n' ' '
